Subject: Pricing metrics clarification — tokens vs characters vs requests

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Acme Health's roadmap for clinical notes summarization. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions on pricing metrics so we can prepare a realistic pilot quote: 

Recap (quick):
- Primary workload: document ingestion -> extractive + abstractive summarization for provider notes.
- Expected volume: ~50k API calls/day initially, with bursts to ~120k/day during peak clinic hours.
- Current telemetry: your instrumentation reports characters and API requests; you don't currently emit token counts.

Main asks / points I promised to follow up on:
1) Tokens vs characters vs requests — what we bill on: Redwood bills on tokens (prompt tokens + completion tokens). Characters are not a billing metric; requests is a useful operational metric but not the unit we price.
2) Prompt caching — if you have stable prefixes (e.g., constant system prompt or repeated patient demographics) we can cache prefixes and reduce billed prompt tokens for repeated requests. Caching reduces billed tokens only when the server can reuse cached KV cache; it does not reduce the stored characters metric.
3) Examples & target unit economics: you asked for a target $/1M tokens — see attached sample calc. For a 1M token baseline we typically target a sticker price range while piloting (example in email).

Quick questions for you so our calc is aligned:
- Can you share: average request length (characters) and an example (one sample request + expected model reply)? If you can export 100 sample requests (anonymized), that helps us estimate tokenization.
- Does the request pattern include many identical system prompts or templates (good candidate for prompt caching)?
- What budget range do you want us to hit for the pilot (monthly committed spend)? You mentioned wanting to stay under $X/month but I want to confirm a numeric target.

Attached: Redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf (pricing tiers) and token_calculation_example.xlsx (worked example showing characters->tokens conversion, and caching savings scenarios).

Next steps:
- If you can send the sample requests (100 anonymized rows) we’ll map to tokens and return a 30-day pilot estimate and proposed $/1M tokens that meets your target budget.
- I’ll loop in Rishi for a short technical sync to validate caching assumptions (15–20 min).

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa

Redwood Inference

Hi Alex —

Great — thanks for the quick responses. Answers below and an example calculation inline so your finance team has something practical to react to.

1) Characters -> tokens:
- Best is a small sample of raw requests (100 rows) so we can run the same tokenizer as the model. If that's not possible, a CSV with representative text samples + character counts works but has more variance. For most English text, tokens ~= 0.75 * characters (very rough). The attached sample workbook runs the exact tokenizer we use and will show you per-request token counts.

2) Prompt caching behavior:
- Caching works when the prefix (system prompt + initial tokens) maps to the same KV cache state. If the template is identical but only names differ, caching usually still helps because names are often in later tokens — the shared prefix is preserved. If the variable text is early in the prompt, caching benefit is reduced.
- In practice, we model three scenarios in the workbook: no caching, 50% effective caching (half the prompt tokens saved), and ideal caching (75% prompt savings).

3) Unit economics / target $/1M tokens example (pilot pricing illustration):
- Example baseline: model A (open-llm-65b-8k) pilot rate = $25 per 1M tokens (intro pilot price, committed volume discount available).
- If your workload averages 1,800 tokens per request (prompt+resp) and 50k req/day -> 90M tokens/day -> 2.7B tokens/month. At $25/1M that’s ~$67.5k/month.
- With 50% prompt caching savings (effective tokens/request -> 1,350), same request volume -> ~67.5M tokens/day -> ~2B tokens/month -> ~$50k/month.
- Important: these numbers are for illustration; we’ll provide a tailored quote after we tokenize your samples.

Next steps I recommend:
- You: share 100 anonymized sample requests (redacted PHI ok) or a small export.
- We: run tokenizer, return a per-request token report + estimated monthly token volume and a pilot quote with target $/1M tokens.
- Optional: run a 2–4 week pilot with a committed spend (example: $40k/month) to validate production numbers; we can offer pilot pricing and negotiate committed rates for long-term.

If it's helpful, I can propose two pricing tiers for the pilot (conservative and optimistic) once we have samples. Also looping Rishi for a short technical call to validate caching feasibility with your engineers — can you share engineering contact(s) for that sync?

Thanks!
Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
